title: Cone-mosaic aliasing sober check — simulate retinal-sampling artifact for geometric hallucinations
note: FROZEN before execution. Motivation: §9.8 (Exp-7 in PERCEIVER dossier) is the cone-mosaic aliasing sobriety check. Williams' groups showed stable 'zebra/hexagonal/periodic' percepts under sober conditions when coherent interference fringes above ocular cut-off (~60+ c/deg) are presented. Hypothesis: most 'stable lattice' drawings in the catalogue (Grove et al. 2026, 10,598 drawings) can be reproduced sober by cone-mosaic aliasing (retinal artifact, not drug). Simulate high-spatial-frequency coherent interference fringes (60–120 c/deg), model expected free-draw responses of sober subjects, and compare against the catalogue.

match_rate.expected: majority (>50%) of catalogue drawings have spatial frequency content in 60-120 c/deg range
match_rate.note: if most drawings match fringe spectra, aliasing is sufficient explanation

aliasing_threshold.expected: 60 c/deg minimum for consistent geometric percepts
aliasing_threshold.note: below 60 c/deg patterns are resolved normally, no aliasing

gates: C1: fringe spectra reproduce within 5% of catalogue geometry frequencies
C2: no drug/psychedelic component in simulation (pure retinal sampling)
C3: contrast-response curve monotonic and physiologically plausible

decision_rule.H0_SUPPORTED: match rate >50% and alien threshold in 60-120 c/deg range
decision_rule.ABNORMAL: some match but below threshold or threshold outside expected range
decision_rule.INCONCLUSIVE: insufficient match or simulation fails gate

implementation_requires: fringe generation module (sinusoidal/hexagonal/random-phase), catalogue frequency analysis, comparison statistics
